heading: Dense and mixture-of-experts models have similar one-job neuron shares, up to trillions of parameters
definition: similar shares hold in other language models, dense and mixture-of-experts, up to trillions of parameters.
summary: So far only the original essay reports similar shares across dense and mixture-of-experts models, and it has no full audit above 100B parameters. Independent studies match only parts of the claim, such as a small uninterpretable share in two dense 7B models, while a Qwen-2.5-32B test found one consistent explanation for only 67.1% of neurons.

suggested_status.by_scale: toy: untested (no key in counts V2.studies_by_size). <1B: no support; only lower shares under other methods (lw:TDqvQFks6TWutJEKu challenges, number quoted second-hand; lw:QwgYmpnMxBZnmGCsw and arXiv:2604.14434 limits_scope). 1-10B: partial independent support for the small uninterpretable share only (arXiv:2602.20904, dense 7B); dense probe results (arXiv:2604.02178) and a Gemma-2B VLA backbone (arXiv:2603.19183) limit scope. 10-100B: R0 for the share (original's Qwen3-32B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B); the same-family test arXiv:2511.06739 gives 67.1%; MoE probe support from arXiv:2604.02178. >100B: untested (no counts key). No study measures a per-neuron share at a stated size above 100B, so 'up to trillions of parameters' has no test; the only evidence the original shows at that scale is one neuron-only Kimi K3 attribution graph, with no ablation reported and no full audit (TITLE:Neural Networks Are Already Clean#R20).
suggested_status.reason: The claim that similar shares hold across dense and MoE models comes only from the original, as one merged row (R9). counts: V2.verdicts.supports.studies 2, V2.verdicts.limits_scope.studies 6, V2.verdicts.challenges.studies 2, V2.studies_supports_only 1, V2.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original 0. Both supports cover only part of the claim. arXiv:2602.20904 matches only the small uninterpretable share (about 6.1% and 5.9%) in two dense 7B Qwen-derived models. arXiv:2604.02178 shows concept concentration in sparse-MoE neurons by probe F1, but the same study finds dense models weaker. The closest same-family test, arXiv:2511.06739, gives 67.1% with one consistent explanation. The two challenges (arXiv:2605.29358, lw:TDqvQFks6TWutJEKu) judge whole neurons with different methods and give no pole-level share, so they are not failed replications of the essay's recipe. That is why the suggestion is not C.
suggested_status.open_questions: What would change the level: (1) an independent pole-level audit with explanations tested on new text, on another dense model and an MoE model, with sample size and error bars; (2) any per-neuron share measured on a model above 100B parameters; (3) separate numbers for Qwen3-32B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B in the original; (4) whether arXiv:2511.06739's 'fuzzy' class counts as one main job; (5) per-neuron job shares (not probe F1) in MoE models. A pole-level audit by another group that finds shares well below 90% in a comparable model would move this toward C.

original_result.setup: Write-ups of 1,000 randomly sampled neurons ('neuron papers'), one per neuron, were produced for Qwen3-32B (dense) and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (mixture-of-experts).
original_result.result: About 90% of neurons had one main job, and the essay calls dense and mixture-of-experts models 'roughly similar'. For models up to trillions of parameters this is only asserted, with no full audit yet of the multi-trillion-parameter Kimi K3.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Only about 6% of neurons in two dense 7B models were judged uninterpretable.
In sparse MoEs, a single neuron often reached near-optimal F1 for most of 58 concepts.
At most 14% of ESM-2-8M residual units per layer matched a known protein concept.
Only 67% of sampled Qwen-2.5-32B neurons got a single consistent explanation.
Only 6 of 20 sampled π0.5-DROID FFN neurons were labelled interpretable.
Only about 15% of experts in a small MoE clearly specialised in one category.
Dense models and Mixtral, the densest MoE, matched concepts to single units worse than sparser MoEs.
Few GPT-2 small neurons ranked top for an Odyssey passage matched its concepts; many seemed polysemantic.
Sampled Claude 3 Sonnet neurons typically fired in multiple unrelated contexts.
The median neuron in a one-layer transformer's MLP got no interpretable hypothesis.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Neuron or pole shares above 100B parameters, including the 'trillions of parameters' part. Kimi K3 appears only through one neuron-only attribution graph, and the original says full audits at that scale have not begun. arXiv:2604.02178 excluded DeepSeek-V3. Claude 3 Sonnet's size is not stated.
untested.basis: counts: V2.studies_by_size has keys 'not stated', '<1B', '1-10B' and '10-100B' only, with no >100B key. Untested-parts lines of TITLE:Neural Networks Are Already Clean and arXiv:2604.02178; problems line of arXiv:2605.29358.

untested.what: A pole-level audit in any model other than the original's, giving the three-way split (one main job / two related jobs / not yet understood). No study in the pack splits positive and negative poles or measures a two-related-jobs share.
untested.basis: Untested-parts lines of arXiv:2511.06739, arXiv:2602.20904, arXiv:2605.29358, lw:TDqvQFks6TWutJEKu, arXiv:2603.19183 and lw:QwgYmpnMxBZnmGCsw. Every tested study's recipe is 'different', except arXiv:2605.29358, which is 'close'.

untested.what: Per-neuron job shares in production-scale MoE language models. MoE evidence in the pack is either single-neuron probe F1 (arXiv:2604.02178) or expert-level output decoding in a 76-84M MoE (arXiv:2604.14434).
untested.basis: counts: V2.coverage_by_operation.probing.by_family lists OLMo, Qwen, GPT-OSS, GLM, Mistral and 'other or not stated'. V2.coverage_by_operation.measurement.by_family lists only 'other or not stated', GPT-2, Claude and Qwen. Untested-parts line of arXiv:2604.02178: no per-neuron job-share estimates.

wording_issues.phrase: similar shares hold in other language models
wording_issues.issue: The shares other groups measure are mostly far below ~90%. Qwen-2.5-32B-Instruct: of all sampled MLP neurons, 20.2% are specific (class 0) and 46.9% are broad with all examples fitting (class 1). Together that is 67.1% with one consistent explanation. The other 32.9% are polysemantic (class 2). All three are shares of all sampled neurons (arXiv:2511.06739 r4-r6, Fig. 1). 76-84M MoE: about 15% clear specialist experts (arXiv:2604.14434 R1). Only the uninterpretable shares of about 6.1% and 5.9% in two dense 7B models are close (arXiv:2602.20904, text). The original itself reports a lower figure for GPT-2 XL: about 70% one thing and about 5% pristine (R8).

arXiv:2604.02178 reports that MoE models beat dense ones in every concept category at k=1, that dense models 'struggle' (r1-r6), and that the densest MoE, Mixtral-8x7B (NA/N=0.25), scores lower than sparser MoEs (r12). On this probe measure, single-neuron cleanliness depends on architecture and routing sparsity rather than being similar. The original's dense and MoE figure is a single merged row (R9, per its verdict fix).

No measured share exists above the original's 32B and 35B-A3B models. The original claims similar results in models 'up to trillions of parameters, like Kimi K3'. It gives no numbers for this and leaves the details to a companion paper. The only Kimi K3 evidence it shows is one neuron-only attribution graph (a found-wallet example), and it says full audits at that scale have not begun. arXiv:2604.02178 excluded DeepSeek-V3. The only production-scale model tested by another group, Claude 3 Sonnet (size not stated), carries a challenges verdict (arXiv:2605.29358 r2).

V2 inherits V1's pole-level three-way scheme, but the studies measure other units and categories. Some judge whole neurons (arXiv:2511.06739, arXiv:2605.29358, lw:TDqvQFks6TWutJEKu). One judges experts (arXiv:2604.14434). One measures single-neuron probe F1 (arXiv:2604.02178). One reports only an 'uninterpretable' category (arXiv:2602.20904). None of them reports a two-related-jobs share.

One model tested against V2 is not a natural-language text model: the vision-language-action model pi0.5, with a Gemma-2B backbone (arXiv:2603.19183 r8). The statement does not say whether such models count as 'language models'.

method_sensitivity.factor: Category boundary for 'one job' (strict vs broad class)
method_sensitivity.what: In Qwen-2.5-32B-Instruct, 20.2% of sampled MLP neurons fall in the strict 'specific' class 0 (r4) and 46.9% in class 1, broad but all examples fit (r5). Together that is 67.1%, the share the verdict counts as one consistent explanation. Both are shares of all sampled neurons. The authors report no test of how sensitive the gpt-5-mini 0/1/2 classification is to its prompt. Their 'subjective and sensitive to prompt verbiage' remark is about the functional categories of Fig. 2, and their Limitations say autointerpretation may miss features' 'true' role. The original says its percentages depend on where the threshold for 'one thing' is set, for example whether closely related idioms are lumped together.

method_sensitivity.factor: Which activating examples are shown (max-activating vs uniformly sampled; top-k only)
method_sensitivity.what: For adapter features, detection scores are 0.82-0.84 with max-activating examples and 0.69-0.73 with uniformly sampled activating examples. The reported neuron score uses max-activating examples. The original says top-k examples alone can mislead because of the negative pole, long context and sign.

method_sensitivity.factor: MoE routing sparsity and probe sparsity k
method_sensitivity.what: Best-layer F1 is compared across routing-sparsity groups (NA/N 0.06, 0.08, 0.12, 0.25). Sparser MoEs give cleaner single-neuron representations, and the densest MoE (Mixtral-8x7B) scores lower. The largest MoE-dense gap is at k=1. Best-layer selection is an upper bound.

In GPT2-SMALL, MLP neurons were searched on one Odyssey snippet with the search filtered to a single layer. Top-25 match counts range from 17 (layer 0, r3; layer 6, r9) to 3 (layer 10, r13). Each count comes from a search of that layer alone, not 'with layer 0 included' as the rows' operation field says. The author says neurons 'fare decently' in layers 6-9. The all-layer top-25 count comes from a different search scope.

method_sensitivity.factor: Unit basis (pole, whole neuron, expert, SAE feature), labelling scheme and pooling
method_sensitivity.what: In pi0.5-DROID (Gemma-2B backbone, layer PG5), 6 of 20 randomly sampled FFN neurons (30%) were labelled interpretable (r8). Under the same temporal-pattern pipeline on mean-pooled activations, 95 of 120 SAE features (79.2%) were. The authors say this matched pipeline isolates the neuron basis from the SAE basis. FFN neurons were sampled in only one model, dataset and layer. SAE shares are 70-90% across six dictionaries, with no causal analysis of model, dataset or layer. Its Limitations say per-token features were generally less interpretable than mean-pooled ones. arXiv:2604.14434 judges experts by decoded output words, not by activations (R1-R4). arXiv:2605.29358 and lw:TDqvQFks6TWutJEKu judge whole neurons against SAE features.

status_amendment.public_note: The size-by-size summary drops a protein-model study that, on checking, does not test this claim, and now says that none of the studies tested against this claim uses toy models and that no study measures neuron shares in models above 100 billion parameters, where the original shows only one example graph. The suggested level is unchanged.
